tweets: Calling external contracts can transfer control to another contract before your function finishes.
This allows a malicious contract to execute code in your function before the original call completes.
Different invocations of your function may then interact in ways you did not intend.
To prevent this, perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
Another common recommendation is using a reentrancy lock such as OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard.
